notes: KAIST Prestige Scholarship (KPS) is a university-wide, automatic award inside the KAIST Scholarship scheme: open to international applicants in Master's-Ph.D. Integrated or Ph.D. programmes across ALL departments, with no supervising professor or research group attached to the award. Selection is by department head recommendation and college dean approval; no named professor appears on the official page. The official_source_url given in the input (…/Scholarship/KPrestige) returns 404; the KPS terms are published on the current official KAIST admissions scholarship page cited in notes, confirmed live. Contact for the programme is the administrative KAIST Office of Admissions (advanced.adm@kaist.ac.kr), not a supervising professor.

The UIC Admissions Scholarship is an undergraduate admission merit award at Underwood International College, Yonsei University. It is granted automatically to newly admitted international undergraduates based on academic credentials and covers full tuition for 4 years. No supervising professor is attached to this bachelor's-level admissions scholarship; the official UIC Tuition fee & Scholarship page lists no faculty or supervisor. Verified live at the official UIC page.

The Yonsei International Companion Scholarship is a Graduate School-wide internal scholarship for full-time international students admitted through the international student admission track. It applies across all departments and programmes with no department-specific supervisor tied to the award; the official Yonsei Graduate School Foreigner Special Scholarship page names no professors (only the administrative mail Ysgrad@yonsei.ac.kr). Verified live at the official page.

KOICA Scholarship Program (CIAT) is a Korean government scheme administered by the Korea International Cooperation Agency (KOICA), a government agency. Consistent with the batch rules for national/government schemes with no attached institution (e.g. GKS/MEXT/Fulbright), no supervising professor enrichment applies. Attempted live verification of the official site (www.koica.go.kr/eng) returned a 'site move'/not-found alert, indicating the English pages are moved/JS-driven; the scheme remains a central government programme, so the outcome is not_applicable.

The GIST Government-sponsored Scholarship is an automatic, university-wide award for all GIST students (government scholarship students receive tuition support and monthly allowances defined centrally by semester limits). It is not attached to any specific department, lab, or supervising professor; the official GIST Government-sponsored Scholarship page lists only amounts and eligibility rules, no faculty. Verified live at the official GIST page.

TU Graz High Potentials is a partner-company-funded scholarship programme for Bachelor's and Master's students across all disciplines, awarded on merit over up to two years. No supervising professor is attached; the official page directs scholarship questions to the administrative office (highpotentialsnoSpam@tugraz.at on the page, an admissions office address rather than a professor's institutional email) and sponsors are companies (APG, GRAWE, NXP, Siemens Energy, etc.), not academic supervisors. Verified live at the official TU Graz page.

The One World Scholarship of the Afro-Asian Institute Salzburg (Archdiocese of Salzburg) is not attached to a single institution or programme: recipients are admitted and enrolled at their own choice of Salzburg university (University of Salzburg, UAS Salzburg, or Mozarteum) in any field, and PhD supervision is confirmed at the student's own university, not by the AAI. The AAI itself is a non-degree-granting institute that provides mentoring through its own staff (e.g. Astrid Schönleitner, Study and Counselling Manager), not professors, so supervisor enrichment is not applicable. Verified live at the official AAI page.
